blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Job evaluation evaluates the worth of a job relative to other jobs within an organization, not the individual holding the position.
Compensation is divided into Direct Compensation (Basic Pay, DA, Incentives) and Indirect Compensation (Fringe Benefits, Statutory Perks).
Point Factor and Factor Comparison methods are quantitative job evaluation techniques, whereas Ranking and Grading are non-quantitative methods.
Compa-ratio measures an individual's salary against the midpoint of the established salary range (Actual Salary / Midpoint Salary).
Statutory benefits in Indian banking are governed by laws such as the Payment of Gratuity Act 1972, EPF Act 1952, and Maternity Benefit Act 1961.

blocks.content: Compensation is the total of all rewards provided to employees in return for their services. It includes both financial and non-financial rewards. Effective compensation management attracts, retains, and motivates employees while managing labour costs.
Job evaluation evaluates the job, not the person performing it.

cells: Core salary for the role; basis for most other calculations; fixed and guaranteed
Compensates for inflation; linked to Consumer Price Index (CPI); mandatory under law for certain sectors; major component in PSB salaries
For accommodation; partially tax-exempt (Income Tax Act); depends on city classification
Industry/employer-specific allowances; transport, medical, telephone, education allowances
Performance-linked; incentive pay; annual bonus; quarterly incentive; profit sharing
Right to buy company shares at predetermined price; long-term retention tool; common in private banks
12% employer contribution + 12% employee contribution; retirement savings; EPF Act 1952
15 days salary per year of service; payable after 5 years; Payment of Gratuity Act 1972; max Rs.20 lakh
Life, health, accident insurance; ESIC for lower salary employees; employer-provided group medical
Casual Leave, Earned Leave, Sick Leave, Maternity Leave; governed by Factories Act, Maternity Benefit Act, and service rules

blocks.content: Job Evaluation is a systematic process to assess the relative worth of jobs within an organisation, primarily to establish an equitable pay structure. It analyses the job :not the job holder.

cells: Rank jobs from most to least important; simplest method; no factor analysis
Simple and quick; subjective; not appropriate for many jobs or large organisations
Pre-define grades/classes; slot jobs into appropriate grades based on overall assessment
Easy to understand; suitable for government; may be arbitrary in classifications
Benchmark jobs compared on 5 factors (skill, mental effort, physical effort, responsibility, working conditions); assign money values to factors
Precise and consistent; complex to develop; difficult to explain to employees
Identify factors (skill, effort, responsibility, conditions); assign points to degree levels within each factor; total points determine grade
Most widely used; objective; transparent; used in government and PSBs; Hay Group method is a variation

items: Formula for Gratuity Calculation under Payment of Gratuity Act 1972: (15 / 26) x Last Drawn Basic Salary & DA x Number of Completed Years of Service.
Distinction between Analytical/Quantitative methods (Point Factor, Factor Comparison) and Non-Analytical/Qualitative methods (Ranking, Classification) is a frequent MCQ topic.
EPF Act 1952 applies to establishments employing 20 or more persons, with statutory employer and employee contributions fixed at 12%.

cells: Group jobs of similar value into grades; salary range (minimum-midpoint-maximum) for each grade; overlap between grades
Minimum and maximum pay for a job grade; allows progression within grade based on performance and experience
Fewer, wider pay bands compared to traditional narrow grades; more flexibility; horizontal career moves rewarded
Variable pay linked to performance ratings or outcomes; merit increase; short-term incentive (STI); long-term incentive (LTI)
Encompasses all direct and indirect compensation + non-financial rewards (career, recognition, work environment)
Employee's current salary / midpoint of pay grade × 100; 100 = at midpoint; above 100 = overpaid relative to market; below 100 = underpaid
Internal equity (fairness across jobs within organisation); External equity (market competitiveness); Individual equity (fairness among individuals in same job)
12% employee + 12% employer (8.33% to EPS-95; 3.67% to EPF); for establishments with 20+ employees; wages up to Rs.15,000 mandatory
15 days salary per year; minimum 5 years continuous service; max Rs.20 lakh; death/disability no 5-year rule
Min 8.33%; max 20% of annual wages; for employees earning up to Rs.21,000/month; must have profit
26 weeks paid leave (extended from 12 weeks) for first 2 children; 12 weeks for 3rd child; crèche facility for 50+ employees; work from home option
Medical, sickness, maternity, disability, dependants' benefits; employee 0.75% + employer 3.25%; for wages up to Rs.21,000
30 days EL per year (banks); encashable; carry forward limits apply; accumulated leave encashable at retirement
Banks covered under Payment of Gratuity Act; some banks offer enhanced gratuity; SBI Act has specific provisions
